title: kbmon --receipt counts no open ask to the operator, so the pane that reads only the receipt shows needs you: 0 while --status all names the ask
goal: kbmon --receipt reads the coord panel too, so its needs you count includes each open ask to the operator and any panel it could not read is named in its not read note, and the line stays within its length bound and unchanged by redact

run: import subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, json; R = os.getcwd(); T = tempfile.mkdtemp(); S = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'c.sqlite'); env = dict(os.environ, KB_COORD_STORE=S); subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', '.'], cwd=T); subprocess.run(['git', '-c', 'user.email=a@b', '-c', 'user.name=n', 'commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'init'], cwd=T); a = subprocess.run([sys.executable, R + '/_tools/kbask.py', '--store', S, 'ask', 'operator', 'Is the sky blue'], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env); r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, R + '/_tools/kbmon.py', '--receipt', '--root', T, '--store', S], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env); line = (json.loads(r.stdout).get('line') if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip().startswith('{') else ''); print(a.returncode, r.returncode, line); sys.exit(0 if a.returncode == 0 and r.returncode == 0 and 'needs you: 1' in line else 1)
